PROGRAM YOUR ROBOT — ACTIVITY 1 (20 minutes)
This is the most important activity in the entire seminar. It creates a visceral, unforgettable experience of what "programming" actually feels like.
ROUND 1 SETUP (1 min): - Groups of 4. Designate one person as "The Robot." Others are "The Programmers." - Programmers cannot speak to the Robot during execution — only hand over the written instructions. - Robot follows instructions LITERALLY. If the instruction says "draw a line" with no direction — robot draws it horizontally. If it says "make a shape with 4 sides" — robot makes a random quadrilateral.
ROUND 1 (8 min): LET THE CHAOS HAPPEN. Walk around the room. Laugh with them. When groups look confused, that's perfect. Don't help. Say: "The confusion is the lesson."
MID-ACTIVITY OBSERVATION: Pick the most chaotic-looking drawing from any group. Hold it up (with the group's permission). SAY: "Behold. The first version of every program ever written."
ROUND 2 (5 min): Tell groups to look at their instructions and fix the specific problems. Give them exactly 5 minutes.
DEBRIEF (4 min — the most important part): SAY: "What happened between Round 1 and Round 2?" Students: "It got better" / "We fixed the instructions" SAY: "That improvement — from broken chaos to something that actually worked — that is DEBUGGING. And debugging is something every programmer, every AI engineer, every data scientist does every single day." SAY: "The algorithm didn't change. The instructions changed. That's what code is — instructions you keep improving until they work."
KEY VOCAB (write on board or say clearly): - Algorithm = A set of step-by-step instructions - Bug = An error in the instructions - Debugging = Finding and fixing bugs - Iteration = Trying, failing, improving, trying again
